messages:
elaine: quick check — i'm seeing a few streaming sessions where the first delta contains a tool_call start but the tool params arrive fragmented across later deltas. is that guaranteed to be okay for clients, or should we enforce an atomic tool_params message?

mike: interesting — i thought streaming could split any field. do we have a spec line about tool_call param atomicity?

ashley: we don't currently guarantee atomicity. streaming deltas are allowed to chunk strings and objects. goal was to keep latency low (send prefix asap).

nav: FWIW some SDKs assume the full tool_call object appears in a single delta and then break when it's split. this breaks our node sdk tests intermittently.

elaine: yeah that's the problem. customers rely on simple reassembly logic. two options: require tool_call.params to be emitted only when complete, or add a stable chunking envelope so clients can reassemble reliably.

sam: +1 on explicit envelope. otherwise every SDK must implement fragile heuristics. what's the tradeoff on latency?

ashley: tradeoff: holding tokens until full params available adds a few ms in pathological cases (long param JSON). but typical tool params are small.

mike: could we do a middle ground: guarantee that when a tool_call starts we always include a small metadata header in the first delta: {"tool_call_id": "uuid", "params_incomplete": true/false}. then subsequent deltas with same id append. that lets clients reassemble reliably.

elaine: love that — minimal change to runtime. will require schema bump (add optional tool_call_id and params_continued boolean). how bad is a schema bump for backwards compat?

ashley: it's additive optional fields — fully backward compatible for strictly-typed clients. the only risk: older clients may ignore id and still assume atomicity. but we can ship a deprecation notice and default to atomic for a short canary window.

nav: timeline? i can add reassembly tests to the JS + python sdks if we land spec this week.

sam: can we get an API governance thumbs-up? @mike can you flag this for the convo contract PR?

mike: pinged in PR #4825 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4825) — description: streaming tool_call chunking envelope. includes example snippets and a migration guide.

pr-bot: PR #4825 opened by mike — reviewers: ashley, nav. CI: unit tests passing, integration failing in node sdk test (reassembly).

ashley: i'll review today. initial comment: we should also document how this interacts with function_call.name vs params ordering. there was ambiguity in earlier threads: if name changes mid-stream, what's authoritative?

elaine: good point. i'd propose: the first seen name for a given tool_call_id is authoritative; if later deltas provide a different name that's a runtime error and should be ignored (and logged). keeps reassembly simple.

nav: +1. i'll add test that simulates out-of-order name change and assert name is sticky to first delta.

sam: what about nullability? should we ever emit null for params vs empty object? cc: SDK folks — clients treat null as meaning no params, empty object as params present.

ashley: spec suggestion: never emit null for params in tool_call envelope. use empty object if there are no params. null reserved for fields we plan to deprecate.

elaine: agree. avoids three-state confusion. also we should add a note on backcompat: older clients expecting atomic tool_call will still work but might see split objects — recommend they adopt the tool_call_id reassembly within 2 weeks.

mike: rollout plan proposal: canary in eu-west-1 for a day with both behaviors: stream with new envelope when enabled via runtime flag, otherwise keep old atomic emission. monitor sdk failures and errorrate. if ok, flip default in 72h.

nav: i'll add a Prometheus metric for tool_call_chunked_count and a debug log for mismatched names.

sam: do we need a client-side opt-in header? e.g., Accept-Encoding: tool_chunking=v1 so clients can declare support?

ashley: optional header is nice but adds complexity to routing. prefer server-side toggle + rollout + clear SDK bump. header could be follow-up.

elaine: ok — action items: mike: finalize PR description + add migration note; ashley: review and update spec doc; nav: sdk tests + metrics; sam: ops run canary and monitor. i'll draft a short note for @customers and for console docs.

mike: one more quick API nit: streaming delta schema currently uses "delta.tool_call.params" as an object. if we add chunking we should allow a string chunk delta too so we can stream large param blobs efficiently. example payload:

```
{ \"delta\": { \"tool_call\": { \"tool_call_id\": \"abc-123\", \"name\": \"lookup_user\", \"params_chunk\": \"{\\\"user\\\":\\\"al...\" , \"params_continued\": true } } }
```

ashley: yeah params_chunk vs params_object is a good design. we'll keep params (object) for complete transmissions and params_chunk (string) for chunks. sdk will either reassemble string and JSON.parse or accept params if present.

nav: will add tests for both chunk types.

pr-bot: CI update: added golden test for streaming chunking in python sdk.

elaine: ok i'm comfortable with plan. if no objections, i'll mark this thread resolved and mike will merge after ashley's review. :thumbsup:

ashley: no objections from me. small request: add an example in the console docs showing client reassembly pseudocode.

mike: will do. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

nav: merging checklist noted. i'll coordinate the canary with ops at 10:00 UTC tomorrow.

elaine: thanks — closing loop. if anyone sees weird failures during canary, ping #incidents immediately.

sam: noted. :eyes:
